paras.en: He joined the company under a vague title, “member of technical staff.” Anthropic declined a request to give further information about his official work. Everyone with second-hand knowledge of the arrangement, however, insists he was not hired to do math.
paras.zh: 他以一个模糊的头衔加入公司：“技术人员”。 Anthropic 拒绝提供有关其官方工作的进一步信息的请求。然而，每个对这一安排有二手了解的人都坚称，他不是被雇来做数学的。

paras.en: But Anthropic employees are allowed to experiment with unreleased versions of Claude in their off time. “Give a math person access to a powerful LLM [large language model] with access to a lot of compute,” says M.I.T. mathematician Andrew Sutherland, “and they will eventually start asking it math questions, whether you want them to or not.”
paras.zh: 但 Anthropic 的员工可以在休息时间尝试未发行的 Claude 版本。麻省理工学院表示：“让数学人员能够接触到强大的 LLM（大型语言模型）并进行大量计算。”数学家安德鲁·萨瑟兰（Andrew Sutherland）表示，“无论你是否愿意，他们最终都会开始问它数学问题。”

paras.en: Alpöge first gained wider recognition on July 19, 2026, with a curt X post at 10:19 P.M. EDT announcing he had solved the Jacobian conjecture, one of math’s most famous problems. Another mathematician, Akhil Mathew of the University of Chicago, had thought that the conjecture might be within reach of cutting-edge AI models and had mentioned it in passing to Alpöge, who took the idea and ran with it.
paras.zh: Alpöge 于 2026 年 7 月 19 日晚上 10:19 发布了一条简短的 X 帖子，首次获得更广泛的认可。 EDT 宣布他解决了雅可比猜想，这是数学最著名的问题之一。另一位数学家、芝加哥大学的阿基尔·马修 (Akhil Mathew) 认为这个猜想可能可以用尖端人工智能模型实现，并在向 Alpöge 提及这一点时，Alpöge 接受了这个想法并付诸实践。

paras.en: This achievement was a turning point, the first really famous math problem AI solved—the sort of thing most people would’ve revealed in a long, explanatory manuscript submitted to a top math journal. To critics, Alpöge’s nonchalant post almost seemed to say, with a callous shrug, “Yup, AI is better than you now.” (Friends say Alpöge now regrets the approach he took, for which a number of prominent mathematicians have castigated him publicly and privately.)
paras.zh: 这一成就是一个转折点，是人工智能解决的第一个真正著名的数学问题——大多数人会在提交给顶级数学期刊的长篇解释性手稿中透露这一点。对于批评者来说，阿尔波格冷漠的帖子几乎像是在冷酷地耸耸肩说：“是的，人工智能现在比你更好。” （朋友们说，阿尔波格现在对他所采取的做法感到后悔，为此，许多著名数学家公开和私下严厉批评了他。）

paras.en: Over the following months, Alpöge repeated this pattern again and again. He’d think of a problem, either because he knew it from his own area of number theory or because another mathematician suggested it. He’d throw his allowance of tokens and an internal version of Claude at it and then inform a few trusted outside experts of what he found. If necessary, he’d iterate based on their feedback.
paras.zh: 在接下来的几个月里，Alpöge 一次又一次重复这种模式。他会想到一个问题，要么是因为他从自己的数论领域知道了这个问题，要么是因为另一位数学家提出了这个问题。他会投入自己的代币和克劳德的内部版本，然后将他的发现告知一些值得信赖的外部专家。如有必要，他会根据他们的反馈进行迭代。

paras.en: These breakthroughs—too numerous and esoteric to concisely list here—spanned a breathtaking range of mathematical topics, more than any single mathematician can productively work in. Of course, Alpöge didn’t need to understand each topic completely. He would act as a kind of liaison between his legions of Claude agents and his human collaborators.
paras.zh: 这些突破数量众多，深奥难懂，无法在这里一一列举，涵盖了令人惊叹的数学主题，超出了任何一个数学家所能有效完成的范围。当然，Alpöge 并不需要完全理解每个主题。他将充当他的克劳德特工军团和他的人类合作者之间的联络人。

paras.en: He’d give his agentic army a direction, often based on the human experts’ guidance, and they’d churn out thousands of pages of calculations, mostly in a math-slop dialect unreadable to any human. But the slop corresponded, in some impenetrable way, to actual mathematical truth. Alpöge’s task was to translate this output, with the help of yet another LLM, into readable math. He’s become a kind of LLM whisperer through this unconventional, somewhat aggravating process, which he calls “AI psychosis,” according to Ethan Sussman, a mathematician at Northwestern University.
paras.zh: 他会给他的代理军队一个方向，通常是根据人类专家的指导，他们会写出数千页的计算结果，大部分是用任何人都无法理解的数学方言。但这个斜率以某种难以理解的方式与实际的数学真理相对应。 Alpöge 的任务是在另一位法学硕士的帮助下将这一输出转化为可读的数学。西北大学数学家伊森·苏斯曼 (Ethan Sussman) 表示，通过这种非传统的、有些令人恼火的过程，他已经成为了一名法学硕士窃窃私语者，他称之为“人工智能精神病”。

paras.en: Still, Alpöge’s correspondents all remark on his shocking ability to grasp subjects far from his expertise—and on his unflagging resolve. “I think he really does understand all this math,” Armstrong says. “He’s like some kind of genius.”
paras.zh: 尽管如此，阿尔波格的记者们都称赞他掌握远离他专业知识的主题的惊人能力，以及他坚定不移的决心。 “我认为他确实理解所有这些数学，”阿姆斯特朗说。 “他就像某种天才。”

paras.en: “He is exceptionally broad,” Sussman agrees. While Sussman is usually the most intense person in his collaborations, “Levent is an order of magnitude more intense than I am,” he says. Alpöge “sets his sights on the goal, and he’s like, ‘I’ll sleep when this is done.’”
paras.zh: “他非常宽广，”萨斯曼表示同意。虽然萨斯曼通常是他合作中最热情的人，但“莱文特的热情比我高一个数量级，”他说。 Alpöge“将目光瞄准了目标，他说，‘完成后我就睡觉了。’”

paras.en: In fact, the issue of Alpöge’s sleep—or lack thereof—is something many of his recent collaborators have noticed with concern. His messages and check-ins, arriving at all hours, seem untethered from any circadian routine. “I don’t know when he’s sleeping,” several of his collaborators told me.
paras.zh: 事实上，阿尔波格的睡眠问题（或者说缺乏睡眠）是他最近的许多合作者都关心的问题。他的信息和报到信息随时都会到达，似乎不受任何昼夜节律的束缚。 “我不知道他什么时候睡觉，”他的几位合作者告诉我。

paras.en: What happened next was a crash. Just as Alpöge was nearing one of math’s loftiest summits, hoping to solve a “million-dollar” problem from the Clay Mathematics Institute’s Millennium Prize list—the highest-value math targets out there—Anthropic’s archrival, OpenAI, swooped in. Rumors had spread that Alpöge and N.Y.U. mathematician Tristan Buckmaster were about to solve the Navier-Stokes problem. Looking for a win, OpenAI’s math team threw colossal amounts of computing power at the problem over several days to get there first.
paras.zh: 接下来发生的是一场车祸。正当 Alpöge 接近数学最高峰之一，希望解决克莱数学研究所千年奖名单上的“百万美元”问题（最高价值的数学目标）时，Anthropic 的主要竞争对手 OpenAI 突然介入。数学家特里斯坦·巴克马斯特即将解决纳维-斯托克斯问题。为了寻求胜利，OpenAI 的数学团队在几天内投入了大量的计算能力来解决这个问题，以便首先实现这一目标。

paras.en: The media painted the controversy as a David versus Goliath narrative. Alpöge did his best to stay out of it and mostly avoided the uproar, while Buckmaster was cast as the human struck down by an iron-fisted tech juggernaut.
paras.zh: 媒体将这场争议描述为大卫与歌利亚的故事。阿尔波格尽最大努力置身事外，基本上避免了骚动，而巴克马斯特则扮演被铁腕科技巨头击倒的人类。

paras.en: A month later OpenAI followed up the Navier-Stokes blockbuster with more than 700 additional results. The proof dump fell upon a mathematical community already in turmoil. It also scooped a number of mathematicians’ progress on important problems, including collaborations with Alpöge that were underway. Any paranoia he already felt was now magnified, and he became increasingly withdrawn, convinced that leaks between the two companies were stealing his progress.
paras.zh: 一个月后，OpenAI 继 Navier-Stokes 的重磅成果之后又推出了 700 多项额外结果。证明转储落在了已经陷入混乱的数学界身上。它还报道了许多数学家在重要问题上的进展，包括正在进行的与 Alpöge 的合作。他已经感觉到的偏执现在被放大了，他变得越来越孤僻，确信两家公司之间的泄密正在窃取他的进步。

paras.en: The most impressive result in OpenAI’s dump, maybe the most impressive AI-powered result up until then, was a proof that made significant progress toward the Riemann hypothesis. This was Alpöge’s favorite problem, the one he’d harbored unspoken dreams of someday besting. Publicly, he posted on X to commend OpenAI’s team for its work. But the very same day, he started poking harder around the edges of the hypothesis with his internal version of Claude.
paras.zh: OpenAI 转储中最令人印象深刻的结果，也许是迄今为止最令人印象深刻的人工智能驱动的结果，是在黎曼假设方面取得重大进展的证明。这是阿尔波格最喜欢的问题，他心中暗暗梦想有一天能打败这个问题。他公开在 X 上发帖赞扬 OpenAI 团队的工作。但就在同一天，他开始用他内心版本的克劳德更努力地探索这个假设的边缘。

paras.en: On October 14 Armstrong sat down on a bench in Alpöge’s hotel lobby in Aspen, Colo.
paras.zh: 10 月 14 日，阿姆斯特朗坐在科罗拉多州阿斯彭 Alpöge 酒店大堂的长凳上。

paras.en: He’d messaged Alpöge, whom he knew was in Aspen for the same secret “AIxMath” conference, because he hadn’t seen him at any of the events. Alpöge said he’d been hiding out in his hotel room and suggested they go for a walk.
paras.zh: 他给 Alpöge 发了消息，他知道 Alpöge 正在阿斯彭参加同一个秘密“AIxMath”会议，因为他在任何活动中都没有见过他。阿尔波格说，他一直躲在酒店房间里，建议他们去散步。

paras.en: The two had only spoken once before, at an N.Y.U. lunch in July. Armstrong was showing Alpöge’s Jacobian conjecture X post on his phone to colleagues around the table. He couldn’t figure out why they were giggling until the stranger with a bowl cut sitting next to him turned and said with a smile, “That was me.”
paras.zh: 两人之前只说过一次话，是在纽约大学。七月的午餐。阿姆斯特朗正在手机上向桌旁的同事展示 Alpöge 的雅可比猜想 X 帖子。他不明白他们为什么咯咯地笑，直到坐在他旁边的那个留着碗形头发的陌生人转过身来，笑着说道：“那是我。”

paras.en: When Alpöge finally emerged in the lobby in October, Armstrong barely recognized him. His hair was shaggier, his facial hair had grown out, and he was cloaked in a baggy hoodie. “He looked ‘like a hobo,’ in his own words,” Armstrong recalls. “He didn’t want to be seen by anyone.”
paras.zh: 当十月份阿尔波格最终出现在大厅时，阿姆斯特朗几乎认不出他了。他的头发更加蓬乱，面部毛发也长出来了，他穿着一件宽松的连帽衫。 “用他自己的话来说，他看起来‘像个流浪汉’，”阿姆斯特朗回忆道。 “他不想被任何人看见。”

paras.en: They strolled through Aspen’s quiet streets for two hours, talking about the Navier-Stokes drama and the powerful, AI-fueled forces that were forging their collective future. This time Alpöge offered no goofy quips, and his frustration was clear. “He’s a very intense person—he’s very moody,” Armstrong says. “He thinks that OpenAI is the evil empire, and he just wants to throw as much sand in their gears as he can.”
paras.zh: 他们在阿斯彭安静的街道上漫步了两个小时，谈论着纳维-斯托克斯的戏剧以及正在塑造他们共同未来的强大的、由人工智能驱动的力量。这次阿尔波格没有提出任何愚蠢的俏皮话，他的挫败感显而易见。 “他是一个非常热情的人——他非常喜怒无常，”阿姆斯特朗说。 “他认为 OpenAI 是邪恶帝国，他只是想尽可能多地往他们的齿轮里扔沙子。”

paras.en: Alpöge doesn’t seem to think Anthropic is perfect either, but he’s glad it exists. When Armstrong complained of math’s fate being in the hands of just two companies, Alpöge replied, “It could be worse. At least there’s not just one.”
paras.zh: Alpöge 似乎也不认为 Anthropic 是完美的，但他很高兴它的存在。当阿姆斯特朗抱怨数学的命运只掌握在两家公司手中时，阿尔波格回答道：“情况可能会更糟。至少不只有一家公司。”

paras.en: Alpöge hadn’t expressed such animosity toward his corporate rivals before this year’s headline-making events, according to everyone I spoke with. But OpenAI’s actions this year, rife with PR-heavy claims and rampant scooping of mathematicians (Alpöge most of all), seems to have made an enemy of him.
paras.zh: 据我采访过的每个人都说，在今年的头条新闻之前，阿尔波格从未对他的企业竞争对手表达过如此敌意。但 OpenAI 今年的行动充满了公关宣传和对数学家（尤其是 Alpöge）的猖獗挖角，似乎已经与他为敌了。

paras.en: Alpöge himself now has no shortage of enemies. In the aftermath of his Riemann proof, he wrote on X, he’s received death threats. And many mathematicians are frustrated with the official narrative, promoted by Alpöge and Anthropic alike, that his math work is merely a “hobby” entirely divorced from his day job—especially when he’s using internal models and resources.
paras.zh: 阿尔波格本人现在也不乏敌人。他在 X 上写道，黎曼证明完成后，他收到了死亡威胁。许多数学家对 Alpöge 和 Anthropic 等公司宣扬的官方说法感到沮丧，即他的数学工作只是一种“爱好”，完全脱离了他的日常工作——尤其是当他使用内部模型和资源时。

paras.en: Three mathematicians uploaded a preprint last week that provides a rare insight into those resources. Alpöge had shared with them the LLM output from one of his summer breakthroughs. They used it to estimate that the discovery—which was several times less ambitious than many of Alpöge’s other projects—cost up to $4 million worth of computing resources. An Anthropic representative declined to comment on the estimate. Whatever Anthropic’s “allowance” for Alpöge is, it’s not an especially cheap one. (Similarly, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman recently acknowledged that costs for his company’s math efforts reached more than $100 million.) For reference, in 2026 the National Science Foundation, the largest U.S. funder of math research, invested about $200 million in the field.
paras.zh: 三位数学家上周上传了一份预印本，提供了对这些资源的罕见见解。 Alpöge 与他们分享了他夏季突破之一的法学硕士成果。他们用它来估计这一发现（比 Alpöge 的许多其他项目要小几倍）花费了价值 400 万美元的计算资源。 Anthropic 的一位代表拒绝对这一估计发表评论。无论 Anthropic 对 Alpöge 的“补贴”是多少，它都不是特别便宜的。 （同样，OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 最近承认，其公司数学研究的成本超过 1 亿美元。）作为参考，2026 年，美国最大的数学研究资助者国家科学基金会在该领域投资了约 2 亿美元。

paras.en: “Anthropic should release how much this costs. How many tens of millions of dollars are in their budget to solve math problems?” says N.Y.U. mathematician Nestor Guillen. In mid-October, Guillen notes, Anthropic and OpenAI each committed $5 million in funding and resources to a joint initiative with the Simons Foundation to help mathematicians understand recent AI breakthroughs. “Would they agree to increase that money to match what they give an employee working on a ‘weekend hobby?’” he asks.
paras.zh: “Anthropic应该公布这需要多少钱。他们的预算中有多少数千万美元用于解决数学问题？”纽约大学说数学家内斯特·吉兰。 Guillen 指出，10 月中旬，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 各自承诺为与西蒙斯基金会的一项联合计划提供 500 万美元的资金和资源，以帮助数学家了解最近的人工智能突破。 “他们会同意增加这笔钱，以匹配他们给予从事‘周末爱好’的员工的钱吗？”他问道。

paras.en: After their afternoon walk in Aspen, Armstrong and Alpöge parted ways, heading back to their respective hotel rooms, where each had a number of agents churning on their current math problems. What Alpöge was working on, he did not disclose.
paras.zh: 下午在阿斯彭散步后，阿姆斯特朗和阿尔波格分道扬镳，回到各自的酒店房间，房间里都有一些特工在忙着解决当前的数学问题。 Alpöge 正在做什么，他没有透露。

paras.en: Alpöge and Claude’s successes on Riemann happened in spurts throughout October and November. In the early hours of November 16, they did the impossible. That was when Alpöge wrote to Anthropic’s CEO Dario Amodei, who asked him to save the announcement until after the company’s initial public offering (IPO) that Friday.
paras.zh: 阿尔波格和克劳德在黎曼问题上的成功在整个 10 月和 11 月期间都取得了突飞猛进的进展。 11 月 16 日凌晨，他们完成了不可能的任务。当时 Alpöge 写信给 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei)，后者要求他将这一公告保留到该公司周五首次公开募股 (IPO) 之后。

paras.en: That day Alpöge visited Princeton University, where he told Bhargava and mathematician Peter Sarnak what he’d accomplished, swearing them to secrecy and asking their advice. “It was surreal,” Sarnak says. “He was in a pretty excited state.” Alpöge spent the rest of the week holed up in Buckmaster’s N.Y.U. office, their old war room during the Navier-Stokes drama, where they now strategized the release of the Riemann proof.
paras.zh: 那天，阿尔波格访问了普林斯顿大学，在那里他告诉巴尔加瓦和数学家彼得·萨纳克他的成就，让他们发誓保密并征求他们的建议。 “这太超现实了，”萨纳克说。 “他当时的状态非常兴奋。”这周剩下的时间里，阿尔波格都躲在巴克马斯特的纽约大学里。办公室，他们在纳维-斯托克斯戏剧中的旧作战室，现在他们在那里制定了发布黎曼证明的策略。

paras.en: Drained but exhilarated, they wrapped up their work early on Friday morning and walked to the touristy Caffe Reggio on MacDougal Street, the only place nearby that was still serving decent coffee past 2 A.M.
paras.zh: 周五一早，他们就结束了工作，虽然筋疲力尽，但仍兴奋不已，步行前往位于麦克杜格尔街 (MacDougal Street) 的旅游胜地雷吉奥咖啡馆 (Caffe Reggio)，这是附近唯一一家在凌晨 2 点过后仍然提供优质咖啡的地方。

paras.en: Love him or hate him, Alpöge has given mathematicians a human face to represent the AI revolution, to project their feelings onto as their world is turned upside down. In his statement about the Riemann proof, Alpöge gave ample praise to Claude—“Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.” But he also highlighted his own agency. “It was my secret in my student days that my plans were for this problem,” he wrote. He used a machine to beat everyone, yes, but he remains a key ingredient. The story he has spun is one of triumphant partnership, portending a bright future for math—a modern retelling of the same “lone genius” story math has always been obsessed with, updated for the AI era.
paras.zh: 不管你爱他还是恨他，Alpöge 为数学家们提供了一张人性化的面孔来代表人工智能革命，让他们在世界发生翻天覆地的变化时投射出他们的感受。在关于黎曼证明的声明中，阿尔波格对克劳德给予了充分的赞扬——“克劳德在终点线附近飞翔、跳舞、闪闪发光。”但他也强调了自己的机构。 “在我学生时代，我的计划就是解决这个问题，这是我的秘密，”他写道。是的，他用机器打败了所有人，但他仍然是一个关键因素。他编造的故事是一个胜利的合作伙伴关系，预示着数学的光明未来——这是对数学一直痴迷的同一个“孤独天才”故事的现代重述，并为人工智能时代进行了更新。

paras.en: Whether he’s a visionary genius or a corporate face, his process and his foibles are a stark glimpse into math’s new, supercharged future—AI psychosis included. Riemann being solved won’t cure cancer or stop global warming. It probably won’t change your life in any noticeable way. But it marks a turning point nonetheless, one whose import will only be fully known to our future selves.
paras.zh: 无论他是一位有远见的天才还是一位企业界人士，他的过程和他的缺点都是数学新的、充满活力的未来的鲜明一瞥——包括人工智能精神病。解决黎曼问题并不能治愈癌症或阻止全球变暖。它可能不会以任何明显的方式改变你的生活。但这仍然标志着一个转折点，其重要性只有我们未来的自己才能完全了解。

paras.en: The upload finished shortly after 8 A.M. on November 20. Alpöge texted Buckmaster the link to his website and instructed him to pass it to Armstrong. “Levent and I always joked, ‘If we ever need anything leaked, we’ll just give it to Scott,’” Buckmaster says. Armstrong posted it to X immediately. It was done.
paras.zh: 上午 8 点刚过，上传就完成了。 11 月 20 日，阿尔波格向巴克马斯特发送了他网站的链接，并指示他将其传递给阿姆斯特朗。 “莱文特和我总是开玩笑说，‘如果我们需要泄露任何东西，我们就把它交给斯科特，’”巴克马斯特说。阿姆斯特朗立即将其发布到 X。事情完成了。

paras.en: But what if there was a bug? Alpöge realized he hadn’t had time to compile the code on his own machine before uploading it. Could something have gotten garbled in the process? People around the world would download his code, and it would crash, making them doubt his claim.
paras.zh: 但如果出现错误怎么办？ Alpöge 意识到他在上传代码之前没有时间在自己的机器上编译代码。在此过程中是否会出现乱码？世界各地的人们都会下载他的代码，但它会崩溃，让他们怀疑他的说法。

paras.en: It was done—the files were already online; the world already informed. But he had to know. Bleary-eyed, he started up his compiler. He could sleep once he knew he’d won.
paras.zh: 完成了——文件已经在线了；世界已经获悉。但他必须知道。他睡眼惺忪地启动了编译器。一旦他知道自己赢了，他就可以睡觉了。

paras.en: *Editor’s Note (11/25/26): This sentence was edited after posting to correct the description of Levent Alpöge’s record in the “pig’s trough” challenge.
paras.zh: *编者注（11/25/26）：这句话是在发帖后编辑的，以更正 Levent Alpöge 在“猪槽”挑战中的记录描述。

articles.title: Do you need to be worried about flying for Thanksgiving this year? We asked the experts

paras.en: The busiest travel days of the year are here, less than two weeks after a historic ground stop, numerous tech and airline outages and swirling questions over what could possibly go wrong now. Ahead of Thanksgiving, we asked experts the question at the top of our family group chats: Will it be safe to fly?
paras.zh: 一年中最繁忙的旅行日即将到来，距离历史性的地面停留不到两周，科技和航空公司出现大量中断，人们对现在可能出现问题的问题产生了疑问。感恩节前夕，我们在家庭群聊中向专家询问了这个问题：飞行安全吗？

paras.en: The short answer is yes, says Arnold Barnett, a statistician at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, who studies aviation. So far this year, roughly 800 million passengers have flown on commercial planes run by U.S. airlines, he says—and each one landed safely.
paras.zh: 麻省理工学院研究航空的统计学家阿诺德·巴尼特说，简短的答案是肯定的。他说，今年到目前为止，大约有 8 亿乘客乘坐美国航空公司运营的商用飞机出行，而且每一位乘客都安全着陆。

paras.en: That includes the recent ground stop on November 13, which the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said was caused by a problem with equipment during repair works at a remote facility that led to widespread communications problems. No air traffic control centers fully lost contact, Barnett points out, and all planes that were in the air during the ground stop landed safely.
paras.zh: 其中包括最近 11 月 13 日的地面停飞，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 表示，此次停飞是由于偏远设施维修期间出现设备问题，导致广泛的通信问题。巴尼特指出，没有空中交通管制中心完全失去联系，并且在地面停留期间在空中的所有飞机都安全着陆。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “Our air traffic controllers and safety professionals are working around the clock to keep Americans moving during what is expected to be the busiest Thanksgiving travel week in 16 years,” said FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford in a statement posted online.
paras.zh: 美国联邦航空局局长布莱恩·贝德福德 (Bryan Bedford) 在网上发布的一份声明中表示：“我们的空中交通管制员和安全专业人员正在全天候工作，以确保美国人在预计将是 16 年来最繁忙的感恩节旅行周期间保持出行。”

paras.en: According to data from the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), which tracks air incidents, 2026 has seen fewer aviation accidents through October than any previous year at that point—1,216 compared with 1,267 in 2025 and more than 13,00 in each previous year, except 2020, which had fewer accidents in the same time frame. Of the accidents recorded through October this year, 244 accidents were fatal and 972 were nonfatal, compared with 240 and 1,027, respectively, in 2025.
paras.zh: 根据跟踪航空事故的美国国家运输安全委员会 (NTSB) 的数据，2026 年 10 月份的航空事故数量比以往任何一年都要少 — — 1,216 起，而 2025 年为 1,267 起，之前每年都超过 13,00 起，但 2020 年除外，2020 年同期事故数量较少。截至今年 10 月记录的事故中，死亡事故为 244 起，非致命事故为 972 起，而 2025 年分别为 240 起和 1,027 起。

paras.en: Indeed, January 2025 saw the first fatal U.S. commercial plane crash in 16 years, when an American Airlines flight collided with a military helicopter over Washington, D.C. The NTSB, which advises the FAA, currently has dozens of open recommendations to increase safety following such aviation incidents.
paras.zh: 事实上，2025 年 1 月，美国航空公司的一架飞机在华盛顿特区上空与一架军用直升机相撞，发生了 16 年来第一起致命的美国商用飞机失事事件。为 FAA 提供建议的 NTSB 目前已提出数十项公开建议，以在发生此类航空事故后提高安全性。

paras.en: David Woods, a U.S. safety systems researcher, says that he trusts commercial planes to carry his grandchildren safely this holiday season—but that this doesn’t mean our aviation systems don’t warrant a critical look moving forward. Woods says he is concerned about so-called reactive safety, or the practice of prioritizing technological innovation and then only adding safety measures once accidents have already happened. The country’s aviation infrastructure is aging, and as it’s updated, officials appear to be prioritizing technological advances such as artificial intelligence over safety needs, he says.
paras.zh: 美国安全系统研究员戴维·伍兹 (David Woods) 表示，他相信商用飞机能够在这个假期安全地载着他的孙子们，但这并不意味着我们的航空系统不值得对未来进行严格的审视。伍兹表示，他担心所谓的反应安全，即优先考虑技术创新，然后在事故发生后才添加安全措施的做法。他说，该国的航空基础设施正在老化，随着基础设施的更新，官员们似乎将人工智能等技术进步置于安全需求之上。

paras.en: “We’re worried on two fronts,” Woods says. “One is that we’re starting to backslide a little on the safety advances, and two is that the changing technology and scale of systems is creating new risks that we’re not seeing and anticipating.”
paras.zh: “我们担心两个方面，”伍兹说。 “一是我们在安全进步方面开始出现一些倒退，二是不断变化的技术和系统规模正在创造我们没有看到和预料到的新风险。”

paras.en: Najmedin Meshkati, an engineering professor at the University of Southern California, who served on an expert panel for the FAA following a fatal crash of a Boeing 737 MAX plane in Indonesia in 2018 and another in Ethiopia in 2019, points out that many aviation accidents happen on the runway—not in the sky. He says that issues with technology and human factors, such as understaffed air traffic control centers, can impact safety. Hundreds of FAA workers were laid off in “Department of Government Efficiency” (U.S. DOGE Service)–related cuts in 2025. The Department of Transportation has tried to bolster hiring for air traffic controllers since then; in response to a request for comment from Scientific American, the department said that no air traffic controllers were cut by DOGE.
paras.zh: 南加州大学工程学教授纳吉梅丁·梅斯卡蒂 (Najmedin Meshkati) 曾在 2018 年印度尼西亚一架波音 737 MAX 飞机和 2019 年埃塞俄比亚一架波音 737 MAX 飞机发生致命坠机事件后担任美国联邦航空局专家小组成员。他指出，许多航空事故都发生在跑道上，而不是天空中。他表示，技术和人为因素问题（例如空中交通管制中心人手不足）可能会影响安全。 2025 年，数百名 FAA 员工因“政府效率部”（美国 DOGE 服务）相关裁员而被解雇。此后，交通部一直试图加强空中交通管制员的招聘；在回应《科学美国人》的置评请求时，该部门表示，没有任何空中交通管制员被 DOGE 解雇。

paras.en: Still, “the recent accidents, close calls and equipment failures are not isolated events,” Meshkati says. “They are symptoms of how people, organizations and technology interact, and fail to interact, in an overstretched system.”
paras.zh: 尽管如此，“最近发生的事故、险情和设备故障并不是孤立事件，”梅斯卡蒂说。 “它们是人、组织和技术在过度拉伸的系统中如何交互以及无法交互的症状。”

articles.title: The hidden math behind this paradoxical Black Friday sale strategy

paras.en: “Found a lower price elsewhere? We’ll match it.” When big-box stores make these promises they sound like they’re on your side. Best Buy, Home Depot and Lowe’s will match prices from Amazon, Walmart and more than a dozen other retailers. Some go even further. Australian hardware giant Bunnings promises to beat any competitor’s lower price by a full 10 percent. In the U.S. Home Depot, Lowe’s and Sears once gave similar offers.
paras.zh: “在其他地方找到更低的价格？我们会匹配的。”当大型商店做出这些承诺时，他们听起来就像是站在你这边的。百思买、家得宝和劳氏将与亚马逊、沃尔玛和其他十几家零售商的价格相匹配。有些甚至更进一步。澳大利亚硬件巨头 Bunnings 承诺将比任何竞争对手的价格低整整 10%。在美国家得宝(Home Depot)，劳氏(Lowe's)和西尔斯(Sears)也曾给出过类似的优惠。

paras.en: But game theory suggests these guarantees are less generous than they appear. In fact, they can paradoxically keep prices high. One telling clue is that many retailers switch off their competitor price matching around Black Friday and Cyber Monday, the most competitive shopping stretch of the year.
paras.zh: 但博弈论表明，这些保证并不像看上去那么慷慨。事实上，他们可能会自相矛盾地保持高价格。一个明显的线索是，许多零售商在黑色星期五和网络星期一（一年中竞争最激烈的购物时段）前后停止了竞争对手的价格匹配。

paras.en: In 1883 French mathematician Joseph Bertrand published a scathing review of a book that offered one of the first mathematical models of economic competition. In that model, rival firms decide how much to produce, and the market settles on what the price is. Bertrand objected by saying that real sellers compete by setting and adapting prices, not production quantities. In just a few sentences, he sketched an argument that still informs how economists think about price competition.
paras.zh: 1883 年，法国数学家约瑟夫·贝特朗 (Joseph Bertrand) 对一本书发表了严厉的评论，该书提供了最早的经济竞争数学模型之一。在该模型中，竞争对手公司决定生产多少，而市场则决定价格。伯特兰反对说，真正的卖家通过设定和调整价格而不是产量来竞争。他仅用几句话就勾勒出一个论点，至今仍然影响着经济学家如何看待价格竞争。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Suppose a retailer called Store A sells a television that costs $500 to buy directly from the manufacturer. If it were the only store selling TVs, it would charge the price that earns it the most money, with no competition to incentivize a lower price." Perhaps $900 marks the store’s sweet spot: enough shoppers will pay that much, but if the cost were any higher, too many would decide the TV wasn’t worth it.
paras.zh: 假设一家名为 A 店的零售商出售一台直接从制造商处购买的电视机，售价为 500 美元。如果它是唯一一家销售电视的商店，它会收取最赚钱的价格，没有竞争来激励更低的价格。”也许 900 美元标志着商店的最佳定价：足够多的购物者愿意支付这么多钱，但如果成本更高，太多人会认为电视不值得。

paras.en: Now introduce a competitor, Store B, carrying the same TV, which also costs it $500. If both stores charge $900, customers might feel indifferent about where to purchase a TV, and the stores will roughly split the sales. But if Store A drops its price to $899, then every bargain hunter will go its way, and Store A will reap all of the profits. In the face of this, Store B drops its price to $898, and so on in a race to the bottom.
paras.zh: 现在介绍一下竞争对手，Store B，也有同样的电视，价格也为 500 美元。如果两家商店都收取 900 美元，顾客可能会觉得去哪里购买电视并不重要，商店就会大致平分销售额。但如果 A 店把价格降到 899 美元，那么每个逢低买进的人就会各走各的，A 店就会获得所有利润。面对这种情况，B 店将价格降至 898 美元，以此类推，竞相降价。

paras.en: Left unchecked, this undercutting would stop only at $500, with neither store earning a dime on the sale. Real prices rarely fall quite that far. Stores differ in location and brand loyalty, shoppers don’t check every ad, and stores eventually learn that if they cut prices once, they’ll have to do so again and again to stay competitive.
paras.zh: 如果不加以控制，这种降价只会止于 500 美元，而且两家商店都不会在促销中赚到一分钱。实际价格很少会下跌那么远。商店的位置和品牌忠诚度各不相同，购物者不会检查每条广告，商店最终会了解到，如果他们降价一次，他们就必须一次又一次地降价以保持竞争力。

paras.en: Yet Bertrand’s core insight still holds: sellers compete via price setting, and the threat of being undercut prevents stores from charging whatever they want. Both stores in the hypothetical scenario would be better off holding at $900, but they don’t. That’s because each worries the other will lower the price, and any agreement to hold the line would amount to price-fixing collusion, which is illegal. It’s a version of the prisoner’s dilemma that happens to benefit consumers. Both sellers fare better when they collude, but they can’t trust each other, so instead they compete. That’s why economists worry about monopolies. A store with no rivals to fear can charge the profit-maximizing $900 and make shoppers either pay above their comfort zone or skip the product altogether.
paras.zh: 然而，伯特兰的核心见解仍然成立：卖家通过定价进行竞争，而被压价的威胁会阻止商店随意收取费用。在假设的情况下，两家商店最好保持 900 美元的价格，但他们没有。这是因为双方都担心对方会降低价格，而任何保留底线的协议都将构成串通定价，这是非法的。这是囚徒困境的一个版本，但恰好对消费者有利。当两个卖家串通时，他们的表现会更好，但他们不能互相信任，所以他们会竞争。这就是经济学家担心垄断的原因。一家没有竞争对手的商店可以收取 900 美元的利润最大化费用，让购物者要么支付超出他们舒适范围的费用，要么完全跳过该产品。

paras.en: Now suppose Store A hangs a sign saying, “We’ll match any competitor’s price.” When Store B considers cutting to $899, the calculation changes. Without Store A’s price-matching offer, Store B’s cut would poach every bargain hunter. Now those shoppers can show Store B’s price at Store A and pay $899 there, so Store B wins no new customers and earns less on the ones it already had. If Store A goes further and promises to beat lower prices from rivals, as some stores do, then Store B’s price cut would actually backfire, sending Store B’s customers to Store A for a better deal. When these guarantees are in place, cutting prices no longer pays, so both stores stay at $900. Without any backroom dealings, the two stores have landed on the price that a monopoly would choose—and the ploy that secured this reads like generosity.
paras.zh: 现在假设 A 商店挂了一个牌子，上面写着：“我们将与任何竞争对手的价格相匹配。”当商店 B 考虑削减至 899 美元时，计算结果发生了变化。如果没有 A 店的价格匹配优惠，B 店的折扣就会挖走每一个讨价还价的人。现在，这些购物者可以在 A 店展示 B 店的价格，并在那里支付 899 美元，因此 B 店没有赢得新客户，并且在现有客户上赚取的收入也减少了。如果 A 店更进一步，承诺以更低的价格打败竞争对手，就像一些商店所做的那样，那么 B 店的降价实际上会适得其反，将 B 店的顾客带到 A 店以获得更优惠的价格。当这些保证到位后，降价就不再划算了，所以两家商店的价格都维持在 900 美元。在没有任何幕后交易的情况下，这两家商店已经确定了垄断者会选择的价格——而确保这一点的策略看起来像是慷慨的。

paras.en: Three things about price matching are worth noticing. First, only one store needs the guarantee—Store A’s promise to match competitors' prices protects Store B’s high price as much as its own. Second, a guarantee that functions as intended almost never gets used. In the idealized model nobody undercuts, so no shopper ever has a lower price to bring to the register. Third, the sign looks like it’s addressed to consumers, but it’s actually a message to rival stores.
paras.zh: 关于价格匹配的三件事值得注意。首先，只有一家商店需要保证——商店 A 承诺与竞争对手的价格保持一致，这既保护了商店 B 的高价格，也保护了商店 B 的高价格。其次，保证功能按预期运行几乎永远不会被使用。在理想化的模型中，没有人会降价，因此购物者不会以更低的价格进入收银台。第三，这个标牌看起来像是针对消费者的，但实际上是向竞争对手商店传达的信息。

paras.en: Shoppers rarely see it this way. A 2003 paper in the Journal of Consumer Psychology tellingly entitled “Failing to Suspect Collusion in Price-Matching Guarantees” concluded that people tend to interpret price-matching offers as a signal that prices are already low, not as a way of keeping them high.
paras.zh: 购物者很少这样看待。 2003 年，《消费者心理学杂志》上发表的一篇题​​为“未能怀疑价格匹配保证中的共谋”的论文引人注目，其结论是，人们倾向于将价格匹配优惠视为价格已经很低的信号，而不是保持价格较高的一种方式。

paras.en: Whether real stores behave in accordance with Bertrand’s model is an empirical question, and the evidence says they often do, under the right conditions. A 1991 study tracked supermarket prices before and after stores adopted price-matching guarantees and found that price matching caused higher prices overall. More recently economist Ran Zhuo examined what happened when big-box chains began promising to match Amazon. Theory predicted that Amazon would stop undercutting—and that’s exactly what Zhuo’s 2017 paper reports. Amazon’s prices rose by roughly six percentage points after the guarantees took effect, according to the paper.
paras.zh: 真实商店的行为是否符合伯特兰模型是一个经验问题，证据表明，在适当的条件下，它们经常这样做。 1991 年的一项研究跟踪了商店采用价格匹配保证前后的超市价格，发现价格匹配导致总体价格上涨。最近，经济学家卓然研究了当大型连锁店开始承诺与亚马逊竞争时会发生什么。 Theory 预测亚马逊将停止低价竞争——而这正是 Zhuo 在 2017 年的论文中所报道的。据该报报道，担保生效后，亚马逊的价格上涨了约六个百分点。

paras.en: Of course, real markets get messy and rarely play out exactly as described in economics textbooks. The effect is strongest under particular conditions: a few big rivals selling identical products where price matches are easy for customers to claim. Economists Morten Hviid and Greg Shaffer showed in 1999 that price-matching offers lose their power when shoppers have to jump through hoops to claim them. Rivals know that few customers will bother, so the threat meant to deter undercutting loses credibility.
paras.zh: 当然，真实的市场会变得混乱，很少会完全按照经济学教科书描述的那样发展。这种效应在特定条件下最为强烈：几个大竞争对手销售相同的产品，而客户很容易声称价格匹配。经济学家 Morten Hviid 和 Greg Shaffer 在 1999 年指出，当购物者必须克服重重困难才能获得价格匹配优惠时，价格匹配优惠就会失去效力。竞争对手知道很少有顾客会打扰，因此旨在阻止低价竞争的威胁失去了可信度。

paras.en: Retailers pitch price-matching guarantees as a promise to make sure you never overpay. But if that were their purpose, then the guarantees would matter most during sales events like Black Friday, when prices swing wildly. Instead that’s exactly when many retailers switch them off. On a normal day a price-matching guarantee discourages rivals from undercutting, so the offer costs stores very little. It works as a threat that rarely gets called. Doorbuster events such as Black Friday and Cyber Monday are all about steep cuts, however, and those cuts will come no matter what, so price matching won’t deter stores from making them. In this setting, price matching wouldn’t operate as a low-cost threat but rather a costly mistake, with stores beholden to every rival’s lowest price. Retailers tend not to explain why they suspend price matching during sales events, yet the timing is telling.
paras.zh: 零售商将价格匹配保证作为确保您永远不会多付钱的承诺。但如果这是他们的目的，那么在黑色星期五等销售活动期间，当价格剧烈波动时，保证就变得最重要。相反，这正是许多零售商关闭它们的时候。在正常情况下，价格匹配保证会阻止竞争对手降价，因此商店的报价成本非常低。它就像一种威胁，但很少被召唤。然而，诸如“黑色星期五”和“网络星期一”之类的重大活动都是大幅降价，而且无论如何，降价都会发生，因此价格匹配不会阻止商店进行降价。在这种情况下，价格匹配不会成为一种低成本威胁，而是一个代价高昂的错误，商店必须遵守每个竞争对手的最低价格。零售商往往不会解释为什么他们在销售活动期间暂停价格匹配，但时机很能说明问题。

paras.en: None of this means you should skip a price match when you find one. If a guarantee saves you money, use it. Just read the offer for what it is: a signal to the store down the street that undercutting won’t pay.
paras.zh: 这些并不意味着您在找到价格匹配时应该跳过价格匹配。如果担保可以为您省钱，请使用它。只需阅读报价内容即可：这是向街上的商店发出的信号，表明降价是不值得的。

articles.title: What helps land recover after fire? This ecologist looks to the past
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: In an increasingly fire-prone western North America, Jennifer Grenz, an ecologist and member of the Lytton First Nation, looks at fire with a holistic eye. She considers her work with landscapes recovering from catastrophic wildfire to be “deliberately unfocused,” spanning soil microbial ecology, restoration ecology, invasion biology and historical biology.
paras.zh: 在越来越容易发生火灾的北美西部，生态学家兼利顿原住民成员詹妮弗·格伦茨 (Jennifer Grenz) 以整体的眼光看待火灾。她认为她对从灾难性野火中恢复的景观的研究“故意没有重点”，涵盖土壤微生物生态学、恢复生态学、入侵生物学和历史生物学。

paras.en: Grenz analyzes historical ecological records, like how Indigenous people have shaped and cared for ecosystems over time, to paint a comprehensive picture. “I’m interested in how those histories leave ecological legacies and hints of the stewardship of the past,” says Grenz, who leads the Indigenous Ecology Lab at the University of British Columbia in Canada. “What changed on the land that made it more vulnerable?”
paras.zh: 格伦茨分析了历史生态记录，例如土著人民如何随着时间的推移塑造和照顾生态系统，以描绘出一幅全面的图景。 “我对这些历史如何留下生态遗产和过去管理的暗示感兴趣，”加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚大学土著生态实验室的负责人格伦茨说。 “这片土地发生了什么变化，使其变得更加脆弱？”

paras.en: Grenz spends time with many kinds of specialists, such as archaeologists, anthropologists and Indigenous elders who provide oral histories.
paras.zh: 格伦茨与许多类型的专家共度时光，例如考古学家、人类学家和提供口述历史的土著长者。

paras.en: Moving forward, her lab will examine ecology below ground, including soil, microbial communities and root networks. The goal is to understand the role of underground ecology in critical topics like carbon sequestration, climate change, biodiversity and sustainable management.
paras.zh: 展望未来，她的实验室将研究地下生态，包括土壤、微生物群落和根系网络。目标是了解地下生态在碳封存、气候变化、生物多样性和可持续管理等关键主题中的作用。

paras.en: “My motivation is in our interior Salish Territories in the southern interior of British Columbia, where my ancestors rest and where my people are,” Grenz says. “The responsibility I feel to them and to our Tmícw, which means our lands, [is] to not take us back to the past, but to show that we have the deep knowledge to help us move forward.”
paras.zh: “我的动机是在不列颠哥伦比亚省南部内陆的萨利什​​领地，那里是我的祖先安息的地方，也是我的人民居住的地方，”格伦茨说。 “我对他们和我们的 Tmícw（这意味着我们的土地）感到的责任是不要让我们回到过去，而是要表明我们拥有深厚的知识来帮助我们前进。”

articles.title: This scientist proves which problems computers can’t solve quickly
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: Dor Minzer remembers sitting in an undergraduate computation class at Tel Aviv University. He was intrigued by his professor and soon found himself pulled into a new world: the mystifying intersection of math and computation, first laid out by Alan Turing during World War II. Working with the professor, Minzer became deeply interested in the limitations of what computers can and can’t do.
paras.zh: 多尔·明泽 (Dor Minzer) 记得参加特拉维夫大学的本科生计算课程。他对教授很感兴趣，很快就发现自己被带入了一个新世界：数学与计算的神秘交叉点，这是阿兰·图灵在二战期间首次提出的。与教授一起工作，明泽对计算机能做什么和不能做什么的局限性产生了浓厚的兴趣。

paras.en: “My part is actually to prove not only do I not know how to do it, but I can prove that it’s impossible,” Minzer says. “You have to really be curious.”
paras.zh: “我的职责实际上是证明我不仅不知道如何做到这一点，而且我可以证明这是不可能的，”明泽说。 “你必须真正感到好奇。”

paras.en: Minzer’s hard work has paid off. In 2018, he proved a theoretical computer science problem called the 2-to-2 games conjecture. It asks whether computers can efficiently distinguish games where almost all rules can be satisfied from those where almost none can be satisfied, when the rules have a strict structure.
paras.zh: 明泽的努力得到了回报。 2018年，他证明了一个名为“2对2博弈猜想”的计算机科学理论问题。它询问当规则具有严格的结构时，计算机是否能够有效区分几乎所有规则都可以满足的游戏和几乎没有规则可以满足的游戏。

paras.en: In September, Minzer and his two graduate students at MIT posted a 95-page milestone paper on the unique games conjecture, which builds off the 2-to-2 conjecture. The paper wasn’t quite ready, but they published to get ahead of a press release from OpenAI, describing its proof for the same problem, slated for only days later. It’s a situation that many mathematicians have found themselves in this year as AI companies flood the field with findings at lightning speed.
paras.zh: 9 月份，明泽和他在麻省理工学院的两名研究生发表了一篇长达 95 页的里程碑式论文，内容涉及独特的游戏猜想，该猜想建立在 2-2 猜想的基础上。这篇论文还没有完全准备好，但他们在 OpenAI 发布新闻稿之前发表，描述了同一问题的证明，该新闻稿定于几天后发布。今年，随着人工智能公司以闪电般的速度将研究成果涌入该领域，许多数学家都遇到了这种情况。

paras.en: Minzer says it’s critical to remember that math, and all the research and contemplation behind it, is very human. “It’s a human activity,” he says. “Research is sort of a living organism, a living body.”
paras.zh: 明泽说，重要的是要记住，数学及其背后的所有研究和思考都是非常人性化的。 “这是一项人类活动，”他说。 “研究是一个活的有机体，一个活的身体。”

paras.en: Minzer teaches his own students now. Some days, he talks to his class and gets the sense that nobody is paying attention. But other days, he gets a few students that participate. They have ideas, they’re excited, and they remind him of his own days as a graduate student.
paras.zh: 明泽现在教自己的学生。有时，他在班上讲话时，会感觉到没有人注意。但其他时候，他也会有一些学生参加。他们有想法，他们很兴奋，他们让他想起自己作为研究生的日子。

paras.en: “I feel like now I feel like I’m passing the torch,” he says. “Before you have a Ph.D. adviser, you’re like a new person in a dark room. There are infinite places to go. Your Ph.D. adviser is the person that holds your hand and says, ‘Okay, let’s walk here.’”
paras.zh: “我觉得现在我正在传递火炬，”他说。 “在没有博士生导师之前，你就像一个黑屋子里的新人。有无数个地方可以去。你的博士生导师就是那个握着你的手说：‘好吧，我们走到这里’的人。”

articles.title: Astronomer Isabel Angelo hunts for odd signals in telescope data
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: Isabel Angelo spends her days searching the cosmos for exoplanets and signs of extraterrestrial intelligence. But Angelo’s head isn’t in the stars. It’s buried under mountains of 0s and 1s — data from space telescopes old and new.
paras.zh: 伊莎贝尔·安吉洛（Isabel Angelo）整天在宇宙中寻找系外行星和外星智慧生物的迹象。但安吉洛的头脑并不在星星上。它被埋在堆积如山的 0 和 1 之下——来自新旧太空望远镜的数据。

paras.en: To piece together a fuller picture of what’s out there (alien megastructures around nearby stars, perhaps?), Angelo and her colleagues at the SETI Institute in Mountain View, Calif., are turning to machine learning models. These tools are analyzing the troves of telescope data for anomalies — things that look “weird” in space that we don’t know how to explain yet.
paras.zh: 为了更全面地了解那里的情况（也许是附近恒星周围的外星巨型结构？），安吉洛和她在加利福尼亚州山景城 SETI 研究所的同事们正在转向机器学习模型。这些工具正在分析大量望远镜数据中的异常现象——那些在太空中看起来“奇怪”但我们还不知道如何解释的东西。

paras.en: Most of the space weirdos will probably turn out to be total normies — a comet, a newborn star or a star surrounded by lots of gas and dust. “These are things that I would expect [the models] to find,” Angelo says. “But the goal is to find something that’s not even in any of these categories.”
paras.zh: 大多数太空怪人可能都是完全正常的——一颗彗星、一颗新生恒星或一颗被大量气体和尘埃包围的恒星。 “这些是我期望[模型]找到的东西，”安吉洛说。 “但我们的目标是找到一些不属于这些类别的东西。”

paras.en: In the meantime, Angelo keeps her whimsy and wonder for space alive by remembering historic moments, like the reveal of the first portrait of a black hole in 2019. The scientists “put all of these telescopes all over the Earth. They wait for the Earth to rotate. They do all this math to construct this one image,” Angelo says. “I can’t believe how creative and innovative we have to be to learn about space. It’s such a specific and really fun challenge.”
paras.zh: 与此同时，安杰洛通过记住历史时刻，比如 2019 年第一张黑洞肖像的揭晓，来保持她对太空的奇思妙想和好奇心。科学家们“将所有这些望远镜放在地球各地。他们等待地球自转。他们进行所有这些数学计算来构建这幅图像，”安杰洛说。 “我不敢相信我们需要多么有创意和创新才能了解太空。这是一个非常具体且非常有趣的挑战。”

articles.title: Quantum Gravity Could Blur The Boundary Between Cause And Effect
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: In classical physics, the rules of causality are imperturbable.
paras.zh: 在经典物理学中，因果关系的规则是不可动摇的。

paras.en: A train can't arrive before it has departed. The consequences of an action must always follow that action, and there are strict limits to how far and how fast its influence can travel.
paras.zh: 火车在出发之前不可能到达。行动的后果必须始终跟随该行动，并且其影响的传播距离和速度受到严格限制。

paras.en: But in the realm governed by quantum interactions, the classical rules can get a little … squishy.
paras.zh: 但在量子相互作用控制的领域，经典规则可能会变得有点……模糊。

paras.en: And if gravity gets involved, things might get downright weird.
paras.zh: 如果涉及重力，事情可能会变得非常奇怪。

paras.en: Now, physicists Giordano Cintia, Federico Piazza, and Samuel Ramos of the Center for Theoretical Physics in France have shown mathematically how quantum fluctuations of gravity could blur the boundaries of cause and effect, turning causality's certainty into a matter of probability.
paras.zh: 现在，法国理论物理中心的物理学家佐丹奴·辛蒂亚（Giordano Cintia）、费德里科·皮亚扎（Federico Piazza）和塞缪尔·拉莫斯（Samuel Ramos）用数学方法展示了引力的量子涨落如何模糊因果关系的界限，将因果关系的确定性变成概率问题。

paras.en: "There is an intrinsic source of uncertainty due to quantum gravity to the exact time at which an information signal reaches its recipient," the researchers told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 研究人员告诉 ScienceAlert：“由于量子引力，信息信号到达接收者的确切时间存在内在的不确定性。”

paras.en: In classical physics, as described in Einstein's theory of special relativity, nothing can travel faster than light in a vacuum.
paras.zh: 在经典物理学中，正如爱因斯坦的狭义相对论所描述的那样，没有什么能比真空中的光传播得更快。

paras.en: That includes information – and anything else that could transport an influence from one event to another.
paras.zh: 这包括信息——以及任何其他可以将影响从一个事件转移到另一个事件的东西。

paras.en: One of the results of this hard speed limit is a set of strict constraints on which events in the Universe can influence each other.
paras.zh: 这种硬性速度限制的结果之一是对宇宙中的事件可以相互影响进行一系列严格的限制。

paras.en: For example, if the Sun is suddenly snuffed out, we cannot know about it until 8 minutes later – the time it takes for the last of its light to travel to Earth.
paras.zh: 例如，如果太阳突然熄灭，我们要等到 8 分钟后才能知道，即太阳最后的光到达地球所需的时间。

paras.en: Or if a star explodes 1,000 light-years away, and you sneeze a second later – the sneeze cannot have been caused by the supernova, even if you have a photic sneeze reflex, because the light from the explosion won't reach Earth for another 1,000 years (minus one second).
paras.zh: 或者，如果一颗恒星在 1,000 光年之外爆炸，而你一秒钟后打了一个喷嚏，那么这个喷嚏不可能是由超新星引起的，即使你有光喷嚏反射，因为爆炸产生的光在另外 1,000 年（减去一秒）内不会到达地球。

paras.en: Physicists represent these constraints using something called a light cone – an imaginary boundary extending through spacetime from a particular event, encompassing all the places that a signal traveling at or below the speed of light could reach.
paras.zh: 物理学家使用称为光锥的东西来表示这些约束，光锥是一种从特定事件开始穿过时空延伸的假想边界，涵盖以光速或低于光速传播的信号可以到达的所有地方。

paras.en: Events inside the future light cone can be influenced by the original event. Events outside it cannot, because doing so would require information to travel faster than light.
paras.zh: 未来光锥内的事件可能会受到原始事件的影响。它之外的事件则不能，因为这样做需要信息传播得比光还快。

paras.en: This extends to Einstein's theory of general relativity, too, even though the geometry is more complicated. Here, spacetime isn't a rigid, unchanging backdrop. Mass and energy curve it gravitationally, bending the paths that light follows – and, consequently, distorting the shape of light cones.
paras.zh: 这也适用于爱因斯坦的广义相对论，尽管几何结构更为复杂。在这里，时空并不是一个僵化的、不变的背景。质量和能量使其在重力作用下弯曲，从而弯曲光所遵循的路径，从而扭曲光锥的形状。

paras.en: But even in curved spacetime, the boundaries of the cones remain precisely defined. Given a particular spacetime geometry, there is no ambiguity about which events can influence which.
paras.zh: 但即使在弯曲的时空中，锥体的边界仍然是精确定义的。给定特定的时空几何形状，哪些事件可以影响哪些事件是明确的。

paras.en: Quantum mechanics operates by a different set of rules.
paras.zh: 量子力学按照一套不同的规则运作。

paras.en: At the Universe's smallest scales, particles and fields can exist in superpositions of different states – combinations of seemingly contradictory possibilities – with their properties described in terms of probabilities rather than definite values.
paras.zh: 在宇宙的最小尺度上，粒子和场可以存在于不同状态的叠加中——看似矛盾的可能性的组合——其属性用概率而不是确定值来描述。

paras.en: And if gravity is quantum in nature, as physicists suspect, then the geometry of spacetime sculpted by that gravity should be subject to those same rules.
paras.zh: 如果正如物理学家所怀疑的那样，引力本质上是量子的，那么由该引力塑造的时空几何结构也应该遵循同样的规则。

paras.en: To investigate what this could mean for causality, Cintia, Piazza, and Ramos used quantum field theory to calculate how fluctuations in the geometry of spacetime could affect the propagation of a light-speed signal.
paras.zh: 为了研究这对因果关系意味着什么，辛蒂亚、皮亚扎和拉莫斯使用量子场论来计算时空几何结构的波动如何影响光速信号的传播。

paras.en: Picture two observers. One is in Marseille and the other in Paris; or one is on the Moon and the other on Mars. Wherever they are, one sends a photon toward the other, who awaits its arrival.
paras.zh: 想象一下两个观察者。一个在马赛，另一个在巴黎；或者一个在月球上，另一个在火星上。无论他们在哪里，一个人都会向另一个人发送一个光子，而另一个人则等待着它的到来。

paras.en: In classical physics, if we know the geometry of spacetime, the departure time, and the speed of light, the arrival time can be calculated precisely.
paras.zh: 在经典物理学中，如果我们知道时空的几何形状、出发时间和光速，就可以精确计算到达时间。

paras.en: But if the spacetime geometry is subject to quantum uncertainty, so too is the photon's arrival time.
paras.zh: 但如果时空几何受到量子不确定性的影响，那么光子的到达时间也会受到影响。

paras.en: "What is physically happening is that the photon travels on a quantum superposition of metrics," the researchers told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 研究人员告诉 ScienceAlert：“物理上发生的情况是，光子在度量的量子叠加上传播。”

paras.en: A metric is a mathematical description of the geometry of spacetime. In effect, rather than traveling through a spacetime with one precisely defined geometry, the photon is traveling through a quantum superposition of different possible geometries.
paras.zh: 度量是时空几何的数学描述。实际上，光子不是穿过具有精确定义的几何形状的时空，而是穿过不同可能几何形状的量子叠加。

paras.en: To understand how the resulting uncertainty builds up over the course of the photon's journey, the researchers examined the effects of gravitons – hypothetical quantum particles that would be to gravity what photons are to light.
paras.zh: 为了了解由此产生的不确定性在光子的旅程过程中是如何产生的，研究人员研究了引力子的影响——引力子是一种假设的量子粒子，它对引力的影响就像光子对光的影响一样。

paras.en: They modeled a signal traveling through a thermal bath of gravitons – a hypothetical environment populated by gravitons with a distribution of energies corresponding to a particular temperature.
paras.zh: 他们模拟了穿过引力子热浴的信号——这是一种由引力子填充的假设环境，其能量分布与特定温度相对应。

paras.en: They found that, rather than averaging out over the course of the signal's journey, the fluctuations produced a cumulative uncertainty that grew with the square root of the time elapsed since its emission.
paras.zh: 他们发现，这些波动不是在信号传播过程中进行平均，而是产生了累积的不确定性，这种不确定性随着信号发射以来经过的时间的平方根而增长。

paras.en: This is characteristic of what's known as a random walk – a succession of random steps that, over time, can take a wanderer increasingly far from their starting point.
paras.zh: 这是所谓的随机游走的特征——随着时间的推移，一系列的随机步骤可以使漫游者离起点越来越远。

paras.en: "A much more naive picture, perhaps suggested by the random walk result, is that the photon bounces against gravitons along its path," the researchers explained.
paras.zh: 研究人员解释说：“随机游走结果可能暗示了一个更为天真的情况，即光子沿其路径与引力子反弹。”

paras.en: The longer the signal travels, the fuzzier the once-sharp borders of the light cone become.
paras.zh: 信号传播的时间越长，曾经尖锐的光锥边界就会变得越模糊。

paras.en: This doesn't necessarily mean that information can travel faster than light, or that effects can precede their causes. Rather, it introduces an intrinsic uncertainty into the boundary between events that can influence each other and those that cannot.
paras.zh: 这并不一定意味着信息可以比光传播得更快，或者结果可以先于原因。相反，它在可以相互影响的事件和不能相互影响的事件之间的界限中引入了内在的不确定性。

paras.en: Under most circumstances, this effect would be vanishingly small. But there is one place in the Universe where the consequences could be profound: the event horizon of a black hole.
paras.zh: 在大多数情况下，这种影响微乎其微。但宇宙中有一个地方可能会产生深远的影响：黑洞的事件视界。

paras.en: According to a prediction made by Stephen Hawking in the 1970s, black holes aren't entirely black. They emit thermal radiation because of quantum effects near the event horizon, slowly losing mass until they could evaporate completely.
paras.zh: 根据史蒂芬·霍金在 20 世纪 70 年代的预测，黑洞并非全黑。由于事件视界附近的量子效应，它们会发出热辐射，慢慢失去质量，直到完全蒸发。

paras.en: That radiation should include gravitons, creating the kind of environment Cintia, Piazza, and Ramos investigated in their calculations.
paras.zh: 这种辐射应该包括引力子，从而创造了辛蒂亚、皮亚扎和拉莫斯在计算中研究的那种环境。

paras.en: But there's something else that makes black holes particularly interesting.
paras.zh: 但还有其他一些东西让黑洞特别有趣。

paras.en: "The horizon of a black hole can be seen as a bundle of light rays kept together by the enormous gravity," the researchers explained.
paras.zh: 研究人员解释说：“黑洞的视界可以看作是由巨大引力聚集在一起的一束光线。”

paras.en: Ordinarily, the uncertainty in the position of a light cone's boundary grows much more slowly than the light cone itself expands.
paras.zh: 通常，光锥边界位置的不确定性增长速度比光锥本身的扩展慢得多。

paras.en: But the event horizon of a black hole is a special kind of causal boundary, defined by light rays that can neither escape the black hole nor plunge deeper into it. And it doesn't expand as time passes in the same way that an ordinary light cone does.
paras.zh: 但黑洞的事件视界是一种特殊的因果边界，由既不能逃离黑洞也不能深入黑洞的光线定义。而且它不会像普通光锥那样随着时间的推移而膨胀。

paras.en: If the quantum uncertainty in the causal boundary's position continues to accumulate, the researchers suggest, it could eventually become comparable to the radius of the event horizon.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，如果因果边界位置的量子不确定性继续累积，它最终可能与事件视界的半径相当。

paras.en: And this is where weird doesn't even begin to cover the consequences.
paras.zh: 这就是奇怪的甚至没有开始涵盖后果的地方。

paras.en: One of the biggest unsolved problems in physics is what's known as the black hole information paradox.
paras.zh: 物理学中最大的未解决问题之一是所谓的黑洞信息悖论。

paras.en: According to general relativity, nothing that crosses the event horizon of a black hole can ever return to the outside Universe. But according to quantum mechanics, information about the physical state of a system cannot be destroyed.
paras.zh: 根据广义相对论，任何穿过黑洞事件视界的东西都无法返回到外部宇宙。但根据量子力学，有关系统物理状态的信息无法被破坏。

paras.en: If a black hole eventually evaporates entirely through Hawking radiation, what happens to all the information about the matter it has swallowed?
paras.zh: 如果黑洞最终通过霍金辐射完全蒸发，那么关于它所吞噬的物质的所有信息会发生什么？

paras.en: In 1993, theoretical physicist Don Page calculated that, under quantum mechanics, information about the material that has fallen into a black hole should start to be recoverable from its Hawking radiation roughly halfway through the black hole's lifetime. That milestone is now known as Page time.
paras.zh: 1993年，理论物理学家唐·佩奇计算出，根据量子力学，落入黑洞的物质的信息应该在黑洞生命周期的大约一半时开始从其霍金辐射中恢复。这个里程碑现在被称为页面时间。

paras.en: But according to Hawking's original calculations, that radiation is purely thermal. It carries no information about the material that fell into the black hole – leaving a big question mark over the mechanism of information escape.
paras.zh: 但根据霍金最初的计算，这种辐射纯粹是热辐射。它不携带有关落入黑洞的物质的信息，这给信息逃逸机制留下了一个很大的问号。

paras.en: When Cintia, Piazza, and Ramos extrapolated their calculations to a black hole, they found that the time it would take for the quantum uncertainty in the position of the event horizon to grow to the size of its radius was of the same order as the Page time.
paras.zh: 当辛蒂亚、皮亚扎和拉莫斯将他们的计算外推到黑洞时，他们发现事件视界位置的量子不确定性增长到其半径大小所需的时间与佩奇时间处于同一量级。

paras.en: So, around the point in a black hole's lifetime when information should start to become recoverable, the distinction between inside and outside the black hole could become profoundly blurred.
paras.zh: 因此，在黑洞生命周期中，当信息开始变得可恢复时，黑洞内部和外部之间的区别可能会变得非常模糊。

paras.en: It's a beautifully neat result, although the researchers caution that their calculations for black holes are, at this time, speculative. They suggest that future experiments using interferometers to measure tiny fluctuations in the travel time of light could offer a way to probe the underlying physics.
paras.zh: 这是一个非常漂亮的结果，尽管研究人员警告说，他们对黑洞的计算目前还只是推测。他们建议，未来使用干涉仪来测量光传播时间的微小波动的实验可以提供一种探索潜在物理现象的方法。

paras.en: "Our mechanism is evocative of the possibility that the general-relativity geometric picture is perhaps classical," they said, "too classical."
paras.zh: 他们说：“我们的机制让人想起广义相对论几何图景也许是经典的可能性，太经典了。”

paras.en: The research has been accepted in Physical Review D and is available on arXiv.
paras.zh: 该研究已被Physical Review D 接受，并可在 arXiv 上获取。

articles.title: Chronic Loneliness Linked to 38% Higher Dementia Risk, But Occasional Loneliness Isn't, Study Finds
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: Feeling lonely now and then is part of life. It can happen after moving somewhere new, losing touch with friends, or spending more time alone than we'd like.
paras.zh: 偶尔感到孤独是生活的一部分。这种情况可能发生在搬到新地方、与朋友失去联系或独处时间超过我们想要的时间之后。

paras.en: Sometimes, the feeling fades when we reconnect with people or find our place in a new environment.
paras.zh: 有时，当我们重新与人联系或在新环境中找到自己的位置时，这种感觉就会消失。

paras.en: A 30-year study of older adults in France, published in Aging & Mental Health, suggests that an occasional lonely day and repeated feelings of loneliness may have different implications for cognitive health.
paras.zh: 发表在《老龄化与心理健康》杂志上的一项针对法国老年人 30 年的研究表明，偶尔的孤独一天和反复的孤独感可能会对认知健康产生不同的影响。

paras.en: People who repeatedly felt lonely had a 38 percent higher risk of developing dementia than those who never reported loneliness. Those who experienced loneliness occasionally showed no significant increase in risk.
paras.zh: 反复感到孤独的人患痴呆症的风险比从未感到孤独的人高出 38%。那些偶尔经历孤独的人并没有表现出风险的显着增加。

paras.en: Previous studies have linked loneliness to dementia, but many measured loneliness only once.
paras.zh: 此前的研究已将孤独感与痴呆症联系起来，但许多研究只测量了一次孤独感。

paras.en: Epidemiologist Yvanna Simon and colleagues at the University of Bordeaux wanted to understand what happened when the feeling continued or disappeared over time.
paras.zh: 波尔多大学的流行病学家伊万娜·西蒙 (Yvanna Simon) 和同事想了解当这种感觉持续或随着时间的推移消失时会发生什么。

paras.en: They turned to the Paquid study, which began following 3,777 adults aged 65 and older in southwestern France in 1988.
paras.zh: 他们求助于 Paquid 研究，该研究于 1988 年开始对法国西南部 3,777 名 65 岁及以上的成年人进行跟踪。

paras.en: For the new analysis, the team selected 1,540 participants who remained free of dementia during the first eight years and had provided enough information about loneliness.
paras.zh: 在新的分析中，研究小组选择了 1,540 名参与者，他们在头八年里没有患痴呆症，并且提供了足够的关于孤独的信息。

paras.en: At four visits over those years, participants were asked whether they had felt lonely during the previous week.
paras.zh: 在这些年的四次访问中，参与者被问及他们在过去一周是否感到孤独。

paras.en: The researchers divided participants into three groups. Some 743 people never reported loneliness. Another 530 reported it at one or two visits, while 267 reported it at three or four visits and were classified as experiencing chronic loneliness.
paras.zh: 研究人员将参与者分为三组。大约 743 人从未报告过孤独感。另有 530 人在一两次就诊时报告了这种情况，而 267 人在三四次就诊时报告了这种情况，并被归类为经历慢性孤独。

paras.en: Over the following 20 years, 560 participants developed dementia. The condition affected 33.1 percent of those who never reported loneliness and a similar 34.5 percent of those who occasionally felt lonely.
paras.zh: 在接下来的 20 年里，560 名参与者患上了痴呆症。 33.1% 的从未表示孤独的人以及 34.5% 偶尔感到孤独的人都受到这种情况的影响。

paras.en: For those experiencing chronic loneliness, the figure climbed to 49.1 percent.
paras.zh: 对于那些长期感到孤独的人来说，这一数字攀升至 49.1%。

paras.en: The higher risk in the chronic loneliness group remained even after the researchers accounted for factors including sex, education, living arrangements, depressive symptoms, and general health.
paras.zh: 即使研究人员考虑了性别、教育、生活安排、抑郁症状和总体健康状况等因素，长期孤独组的风险仍然较高。

paras.en: The researchers also examined a smaller group of 217 people whose loneliness appeared to disappear. They had reported loneliness at just one of the first three visits and no longer felt lonely at the final assessment.
paras.zh: 研究人员还对一小部分 217 人进行了检查，他们的孤独感似乎消失了。他们在前三次访问中只有一次报告感到孤独，而在最后的评估中不再感到孤独。

paras.en: This group showed a tendency toward lower dementia risk than people who never reported loneliness, though the difference wasn't statistically significant.
paras.zh: 与从未报告过孤独的人相比，这一组人表现出患痴呆症的风险较低的趋势，尽管差异在统计上并不显着。

paras.en: The association with dementia remained after researchers accounted for whether participants lived alone. About 70 percent of those experiencing chronic loneliness lived alone, but the remaining 30 percent shared a home with someone.
paras.zh: 在研究人员考虑了参与者是否独居后，与痴呆症的关联仍然存在。大约 70% 经历长期孤独的人独居，但剩下的 30% 与某人同住一个家。

paras.en: "These findings confirmed that chronic loneliness is not only a social concern but is associated to an accelerated brain aging, with far-reaching implications for dementia prevention," Simon and team write.
paras.zh: 西蒙和团队写道：“这些发现证实，长期孤独不仅是一个社会问题，而且与大脑加速老化有关，对预防痴呆症具有深远影响。”

paras.en: Loneliness is complex. Someone can live independently and maintain fulfilling relationships. Another person might spend every day surrounded by family yet still feel disconnected.
paras.zh: 孤独是复杂的。有人可以独立生活并维持令人满意的关系。另一个人可能每天都被家人包围，但仍然感到与世隔绝。

paras.en: Why persistent feelings of loneliness might affect the brain isn't yet clear. One possible explanation involves stress. Feeling lonely can activate the body's stress-response systems. When loneliness persists, those systems may remain active for longer.
paras.zh: 为什么持续的孤独感可能会影响大脑目前尚不清楚。一种可能的解释涉及压力。孤独感会激活身体的压力反应系统。当孤独持续存在时，这些系统可能会保持活跃更长时间。

paras.en: Earlier research has associated loneliness with inflammation, changes in immune activity, and biological processes that could affect brain health.
paras.zh: 早期的研究将孤独与炎症、免疫活动的变化以及可能影响大脑健康的生物过程联系起来。

paras.en: Persistent loneliness may also shape everyday behavior, potentially reducing physical activity and opportunities for mentally stimulating social interaction.
paras.zh: 持续的孤独感还可能影响日常行为，可能会减少体力活动和精神刺激社交互动的机会。

paras.en: Asking older adults about loneliness may be useful, even when they live with other people.
paras.zh: 向老年人询问孤独感可能会很有用，即使他们与其他人住在一起。

paras.en: Meaningful relationships, community activities, and regular social contact may help people feel more connected.
paras.zh: 有意义的关系、社区活动和定期的社交接触可以帮助人们感觉更紧密的联系。

paras.en: There are important uncertainties, however. The researchers didn't directly test the proposed biological mechanisms or whether social activities could prevent dementia.
paras.zh: 然而，存在重要的不确定性。研究人员没有直接测试所提出的生物机制或社交活动是否可以预防痴呆症。

paras.en: Loneliness was measured using one question about the previous week at visits several years apart, meaning changes between assessments could have been missed. The analysis also excluded people who died or developed dementia during the initial eight years, which the authors say may have led them to underestimate the link.
paras.zh: 孤独感是在相隔数年的访问中使用有关前一周的一个问题来衡量的，这意味着评估之间的变化可能会被忽略。该分析还排除了在最初八年中死亡或患痴呆症的人，作者说这可能导致他们低估了这种联系。

paras.en: Because the study was observational, it can't prove that loneliness causes dementia. Early changes in brain health could also influence feelings of loneliness.
paras.zh: 由于该研究是观察性的，因此无法证明孤独会导致痴呆症。大脑健康的早期变化也可能影响孤独感。

paras.en: To explore whether early cognitive changes might explain the association, the researchers repeated their analysis after excluding 405 participants with mild cognitive impairment, a condition involving memory or thinking problems greater than expected for their age.
paras.zh: 为了探讨早期认知变化是否可以解释这种关联，研究人员在排除了 405 名患有轻度认知障碍的参与者后重复了他们的分析，轻度认知障碍是一种涉及记忆或思维问题的疾病，其程度超出了其年龄的预期。

paras.en: The association with chronic loneliness remained.
paras.zh: 与长期孤独的联系仍然存在。

paras.en: "As some situations of loneliness are a potentially preventable or reversible condition," the study authors conclude, "it may represent [a critical and actionable] target for interventions aimed at promoting healthy cognitive aging, preserving autonomy, and improving quality of life in later adulthood."
paras.zh: 研究作者总结道：“由于某些孤独状况是一种潜在的可预防或可逆转的状况，因此它可能代表了旨在促进健康的认知衰老、保持自主性和提高成年后期生活质量的干预措施的[一个关键且可操作的]目标。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Aging & Mental Health..
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《老龄化与心理健康》杂志上。

articles.title: A World-First Trial Injected Stem Cells Into The Brains of Alzheimer's Patients, With Positive Early Results
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: You only need to take a look at the risk factors for Alzheimer's – sleep quality, eyesight, air pollution, diet, reading habits, genetics, and mental health to name just seven – to realize what a complex and difficult disease this is.
paras.zh: 您只需看看阿尔茨海默病的危险因素——睡眠质量、视力、空气污染、饮食、阅读习惯、遗传和心理健康仅举七个——就可以认识到这是一种多么复杂和困难的疾病。

paras.en: That complexity means researchers are attacking the disease from all angles when it comes to potential treatments, and there are promising early results to report from a recent Phase 1 clinical trial, summarized in a brief abstract at Alzheimer's & Dementia.
paras.zh: 这种复杂性意味着研究人员在寻找潜在的治疗方法时正在从各个角度攻击这种疾病，并且最近的一期临床试验报告了有希望的早期结果，《阿尔茨海默氏症和痴呆症》的简短摘要对此进行了总结。

paras.en: The trial was led by a team from Regeneration Biomedical Inc (RBI), a pharmaceutical company that's behind the new therapy, which uses patients' own stem cells – regenerative cells that can turn into many other types of cells – to clear away some of the toxic build-up in neurons that characterizes Alzheimer's.
paras.zh: 该试验由再生生物医学公司（RBI）的一个团队领导，该公司是一家制药公司，该公司是新疗法的幕后推手，该疗法使用患者自身的干细胞（可以转变为许多其他类型细胞的再生细胞）来清除阿尔茨海默氏症特征的神经元中积聚的一些有毒物质。

paras.en: Not only was the treatment shown to be safe in five participants in the Phase 1 trial, but there were positive early signs in terms of cognitive improvements. A more comprehensive Phase 2 trial is scheduled to get underway very soon.
paras.zh: 第一阶段试验中的五名参与者不仅被证明该治疗是安全的，而且在认知改善方面也出现了积极的早期迹象。更全面的第二阶段试验计划很快开始。

paras.en: "Our direct-to-brain platform is designed to bypass the blood-brain barrier and deliver a patient's own stem cells throughout the central nervous system," says neurosurgeon Christopher Duma, the founder and president of RBI.
paras.zh: RBI 创始人兼总裁、神经外科医生克里斯托弗·杜马 (Christopher Duma) 表示：“我们的直接大脑平台旨在绕过血脑屏障，将患者自身的干细胞输送到整个中枢神经系统。”

paras.en: "We believe Alzheimer's disease is a whole-brain disorder requiring a comprehensive therapeutic approach – one capable of influencing neuroinflammation, tau biology, amyloid processing, and neuronal health simultaneously."
paras.zh: “我们相信阿尔茨海默病是一种全脑疾病，需要综合的治疗方法——一种能够同时影响神经炎症、tau 蛋白生物学、淀粉样蛋白加工和神经元健康的方法。”

paras.en: Here's how the treatment (RB-ADSC) works: stem cells from a patient's body fat are extracted and 'supercharged' using a family of proteins known as Wnt, which act as chemical messengers telling other cells to grow and repair themselves.
paras.zh: 该疗法 (RB-ADSC) 的工作原理如下：从患者体内的脂肪中提取干细胞，并使用名为 Wnt 的蛋白质家族进行“增压”，Wnt 蛋白质充当化学信使，告诉其他细胞生长和自我修复。

paras.en: These stem cells are then piped down from a surgical implant to fluid-filled areas of the brain called ventricles, which then, in theory, rejuvenate the brain's own repair and waste management systems.
paras.zh: 然后，这些干细胞从手术植入物输送到大脑中充满液体的区域（称为脑室），理论上，脑室的修复和废物管理系统将恢复活力。

paras.en: The aim is to repair broken neurons, reduce inflammation, and clear out the harmful amyloid-beta and tau protein build-up that comes along with Alzheimer's, all through a single therapy.
paras.zh: 其目的是通过单一疗法修复受损的神经元、减少炎症并清除阿尔茨海默氏症带来的有害的β-淀粉样蛋白和tau蛋白积聚。

paras.en: As well as sweeping away toxic proteins, as other treatments do, RB-ADSC aims to repair the processes creating them.
paras.zh: 与其他治疗方法一样，RB-ADSC 不仅清除有毒蛋白质，还旨在修复产生有毒蛋白质的过程。

paras.en: "If you have a refrigerator and it's producing spoiled food, why would you keep removing the spoiled food instead of fixing the refrigerator?" says Duma.
paras.zh: “如果你有一台冰箱，并且它正在生产变质的食物，你为什么要不断地清除变质的食物而不是修理冰箱呢？”杜马说。

paras.en: "Our hypothesis is you have to fix what's going wrong in the brain."
paras.zh: “我们的假设是你必须修复大脑中出现的问题。”

paras.en: The primary purpose of a Phase 1 trial is to establish safety, hence the low number of participants. However, in addition to demonstrating that there were no serious side effects, the trial results recorded cognitive improvements in four out of five of the volunteers.
paras.zh: 第一阶段试验的主要目的是确定安全性，因此参与者人数较少。然而，除了证明没有严重的副作用之外，试验结果还记录了五分之四的志愿者的认知能力改善。

paras.en: It means that the research can now progress to a Phase 2 trial, where RB-ADSC will be tested in 115 participants and put up against a placebo. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in the US has approved 'fast track' status for the next stage, which means testing and reviewing can happen more quickly.
paras.zh: 这意味着该研究现在可以进入第二阶段试验，其中 RB-ADSC 将在 115 名参与者中进行测试，并与安慰剂进行对比。美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 已批准下一阶段的“快速通道”状态，这意味着测试和审查可以更快地进行。

paras.en: "We believe this designation recognizes the urgent need for innovative therapies that address Alzheimer's disease through mechanisms beyond any single pathological pathway," says Duma.
paras.zh: 杜马说：“我们相信这一称号认识到迫切需要通过超越任何单一病理途径的机制来解决阿尔茨海默病的创新疗法。”

paras.en: The next stage of the research will look more closely at improvements in brain function and cognition, as well as the effect the Wnt-charged stem cells have on toxic amyloid-beta and tau protein clumps.
paras.zh: 研究的下一阶段将更密切地关注大脑功能和认知的改善，以及带 Wnt 的干细胞对有毒的 β 淀粉样蛋白和 tau 蛋白团块的影响。

paras.en: According to the latest information from RBI, the Phase 2 trial could get underway as early as December, though it's likely to be several years before we get confirmed results.
paras.zh: 根据 RBI 的最新信息，第二阶段试验最早可能在 12 月开始，尽管我们可能需要几年时间才能得到确认的结果。

paras.en: It's an exciting addition to the growing number of treatment options being analyzed by researchers in recent years, getting us gradually closer and closer to the point of being able to stop, reverse, and prevent Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 近年来，研究人员正在分析越来越多的治疗方案，这是一个令人兴奋的补充，使我们逐渐接近能够阻止、逆转和预防阿尔茨海默病的目标。

paras.en: "Our first-in-human stem cell trial demonstrated favorable safety and statistically significant biomarker changes through 52 weeks," says Duma. "FDA Fast Track Designation marks an exciting step toward Phase 2."
paras.zh: “我们的首次人体干细胞试验证明了良好的安全性，并且在 52 周内生物标志物发生了显着的变化，”Duma 说。 “FDA 快速通道指定标志着迈向第二阶段的激动人心的一步。”

paras.en: An abstract summarizing the results of the phase 1 trial has been published in Alzheimer's & Dementia.
paras.zh: 总结第一阶段试验结果的摘要已发表在《阿尔茨海默病与痴呆》杂志上。

articles.title: The surprising reason women seem better at multitasking than men

paras.en: The surprising reason women seem better at multitasking than men
paras.zh: 女性似乎比男性更擅长同时处理多项任务的令人惊讶的原因

paras.en: Men and women appear to be similarly capable of multitasking, but men are more than twice as likely to ignore conversation while juggling multiple activities. Researchers believe this unexpected difference may help explain why women are widely perceived as better multitaskers.
paras.zh: 男性和女性似乎具有相似的多任务处理能力，但男性在兼顾多项活动时忽视对话的可能性是男性的两倍多。研究人员认为，这种意想不到的差异可能有助于解释为什么女性被广泛认为是更好的多任务处理者。

paras.en: Men and women appear to be similarly skilled at juggling multiple activities, but new research has uncovered one striking difference. In an experiment designed to recreate the demands of everyday life, men ignored conversational questions more than twice as often as women while performing just as well on the other tasks.
paras.zh: 男性和女性在处理多项活动方面似乎有着相似的能力，但新的研究发现了一个显着的差异。在一项旨在重现日常生活需求的实验中，男性忽略对话问题的频率是女性的两倍多，而在其他任务上的表现却与女性一样好。

paras.en: Whether driving, working, doing household chores, or enjoying leisure activities, people frequently find themselves managing several tasks at once or switching between them. Although women are widely believed to be better at multitasking than men, previous research has found only minor and inconsistent differences between the sexes, raising doubts about the accuracy of this popular assumption.
paras.zh: 无论是开车、工作、做家务还是享受休闲活动，人们经常发现自己同时处理多项任务或在这些任务之间切换。尽管人们普遍认为女性比男性更擅长同时处理多项任务，但之前的研究发现，两性之间只有微小且不一致的差异，这引发了人们对这一流行假设的准确性的怀疑。

paras.en: With support from the Bial Foundation, researchers André and Diana Szameitat (from Brunel University of London and City St George's, University of London, UK, respectively) set out to determine whether meaningful differences exist in multitasking ability and what might explain the widespread belief that women have an advantage.
paras.zh: 在 Bial 基金会的支持下，研究人员 André 和 Diana Szameitat（分别来自伦敦布鲁内尔大学和英国伦敦大学圣乔治城分校）着手确定多任务处理能力是否存在有意义的差异，以及如何解释人们普遍认为女性具有优势的观点。

paras.en: In their study, "Men Talk Less Than Women During Multitasking," published in the scientific journal Psychological Research, the researchers developed an experiment involving five different activities. The setup was designed to capture the complexity of everyday multitasking more accurately than most previous studies.
paras.zh: 在他们的研究中，研究人员发表在科学杂志《心理学研究》上的《多任务处理期间男性说话少于女性》中，研究人员开展了一项涉及五种不同活动的实验。该设置旨在比之前的大多数研究更准确地捕捉日常多任务处理的复杂性。

paras.en: The first experiment involved 41 men and 37 women. Participants were asked to follow a recipe in a kitchen setting, look up phone numbers, match numbers with letters, watch a slideshow for specific words, and answer conversational questions. A new question was posed every 20 seconds (e.g., "Would you rather lose all of your money and valuables or all of the pictures you have ever taken, and why?").
paras.zh: 第一个实验涉及 41 名男性和 37 名女性。参与者被要求在厨房环境中遵循食谱、查找电话号码、将数字与字母匹配、观看幻灯片以查找特定单词，并回答对话问题。每 20 秒就会提出一个新问题（例如，“您愿意失去所有金钱和贵重物品，还是丢失所有拍摄过的照片，为什么？”）。

paras.en: In a second experiment, the researchers recruited 160 observers to determine whether differences in multitasking behavior were noticeable to others. Without being given prior information about the participants or findings, the observers watched video recordings of the experiments and assessed how well the participants performed.
paras.zh: 在第二个实验中，研究人员招募了 160 名观察者来确定其他人是否能注意到多任务处理行为的差异。在没有事先获得有关参与者或研究结果的信息的情况下，观察者观看了实验的视频记录并评估了参与者的表现。

paras.en: One Surprising Difference Between Men and Women
paras.zh: 男性和女性之间的一个令人惊讶的差异

paras.en: Men and women achieved comparable results on four of the five activities. Conversation, however, revealed a notable exception. Men left conversational questions unanswered more than twice as often as women. When men did answer, their responses were just as fast and of comparable quality to those given by women.
paras.zh: 男性和女性在五项活动中的四项上取得了可比的结果。然而，谈话却揭示了一个值得注意的例外。男性未回答对话问题的频率是女性的两倍多。当男性做出回答时，他们的反应速度和质量与女性的反应相当。

paras.en: The researchers suggest that women may, on average, be more inclined to engage in communication during social interactions. However, the study did not directly investigate this possibility, so the explanation should be treated with caution. The results are also consistent with evolutionary theories suggesting that women may have a greater tendency to engage in conversation.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，平均而言，女性可能更倾向于在社交互动中进行交流。然而，该研究并没有直接调查这种可能性，因此应谨慎对待这一解释。研究结果也与进化论相一致，进化论表明女性可能更倾向于参与对话。

paras.en: How Conversation Shapes Perceptions of Ability
paras.zh: 对话如何塑造对能力的看法

paras.en: The differences in conversational engagement appeared to have a considerable impact on how others judged the participants. Observers rated men as having less control over the activities, performing more poorly, putting in less effort, and being less alert than women. They also perceived men as less happy and as deriving less enjoyment from the experience.
paras.zh: 对话参与度的差异似乎对其他人如何评价参与者有相当大的影响。观察家认为，与女性相比，男性对活动的控制能力较差，表现更差，付出的努力更少，而且不够警觉。他们还认为男性不那么快乐，从经历中获得的乐趣也更少。

paras.en: Rather than revealing a broad difference in multitasking ability between men and women, the research points to a much more specific behavioral distinction: men are more likely to leave conversations unanswered when managing several activities simultaneously.
paras.zh: 该研究并没有揭示男性和女性在多任务处理能力上的广泛差异，而是指出了一种更具体的行为差异：男性在同时管理多项活动时更有可能不回答对话。

paras.en: Because conversational engagement is easily noticed by others, this difference may create the impression that men are less effective at multitasking, even when their performance on other activities is comparable to that of women. The findings offer a potential explanation for how the popular stereotype that women are better multitaskers developed and why it continues to persist.
paras.zh: 由于对话参与很容易被其他人注意到，因此这种差异可能会给人留下这样的印象：男性在多任务处理方面效率较低，即使他们在其他活动上的表现与女性相当。这些发现为人们普遍认为女性更擅长多任务处理的刻板印象是如何形成以及为何持续存在提供了一个潜在的解释。

paras.en: "Taken together, our data confirm that there are no substantial sex differences in cognitive visual-manual tasks, but that significant sex differences do exist in the ability to hold a conversation while multitasking," explains André Szameitat. This is "an ability highly salient in everyday life and, thus, could explain the development of the widespread public stereotype that women are better at multitasking than men," the researcher concludes.
paras.zh: “总而言之，我们的数据证实，在认知视觉手动任务中不存在显着的性别差异，但在多任务处理时进行对话的能力确实存在显着的性别差异，”André Szameitat 解释道。研究人员总结道，这是“一种在日常生活中非常突出的能力，因此可以解释为什么公众普遍认为女性比男性更擅长同时处理多项任务”。

paras.en: Materials provided by BIAL Foundation. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由 BIAL 基金会提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - AndrÃ© J. Szameitat, Diana P. Szameitat. Men talk less than women during multitasking. Psychological Research, 2026; 90 (3) DOI: 10.1007/s00426-026-02279-5
paras.zh: - 安德烈·J·萨梅塔特、戴安娜·P·萨梅塔特。在同时处理多项任务时，男性比女性说话少。心理学研究，2026； 90 (3) DOI: 10.1007/s00426-026-02279-5

articles.title: Loneliness is making us sick, but we may be treating it all wrong

paras.en: Loneliness is making us sick, but we may be treating it all wrong
paras.zh: 孤独让我们生病，但我们可能对待它的方式都是错误的

paras.en: Loneliness can be surprisingly deadly, with previous research linking it to a roughly 30% increase in the risk of premature death. However, a new study warns that treating loneliness as a medical condition could distract from its deeper social causes. While healthcare professionals can offer support, lasting solutions may require rebuilding communities and fundamentally changing the way people live and work.
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的是，孤独可能是致命的，之前的研究表明孤独会使过早死亡的风险增加约 30%。然而，一项新的研究警告说，将孤独视为一种医疗状况可能会分散人们对其更深层次社会原因的注意力。虽然医疗保健专业人员可以提供支持，但持久的解决方案可能需要重建社区并从根本上改变人们的生活和工作方式。

paras.en: Research has established that loneliness can have serious consequences for physical health. However, a new University of Michigan study warns that treating loneliness primarily as a health problem could shift responsibility away from society and place it on a healthcare system that lacks the tools to restore meaningful social connections.
paras.zh: 研究表明，孤独会对身体健康产生严重后果。然而，密歇根大学的一项新研究警告说，将孤独主要视为健康问题可能会将责任从社会转移到缺乏恢复有意义的社会联系工具的医疗保健系统上。

paras.en: Published in Social Problems, the study examines how chronic loneliness and social isolation became recognized as major public health concerns after researchers uncovered links to illness, premature death, and increased healthcare spending.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《社会问题》杂志上，探讨了在研究人员发现慢性孤独和社会孤立与疾病、过早死亡和医疗支出增加之间的联系后，慢性孤独和社会孤立如何被认为是主要的公共卫生问题。

paras.en: Previous studies highlighted in the research illustrate the severity of these consequences. One estimated that lacking social connections could be as harmful to health as smoking 15 cigarettes a day. Another found that loneliness, social isolation, and living alone were each associated with an approximately 30% higher risk of premature death. The financial burden is also substantial, with separate research estimating that social isolation costs Medicare $6.7 billion each year in care for older adults.
paras.zh: 该研究中强调的先前研究说明了这些后果的严重性。有人估计，缺乏社交关系对健康的危害与每天吸 15 支烟一样。另一项研究发现，孤独、社会孤立和独居均与过早死亡风险增加约 30% 相关。经济负担也很重，另一项研究估计，医疗保险每年因社会孤立而花费 67 亿美元来照顾老年人。

paras.en: "Once people saw these findings, they began to treat loneliness as urgent," said University of Michigan doctoral student Sofia Hiltner. "But it made me wonder: Why do we only consider problems important once they are tied to health?"
paras.zh: 密歇根大学博士生索菲亚希尔特纳说：“一旦人们看到这些发现，他们就开始将孤独视为紧迫问题。” “但这让我想知道：为什么我们只有在问题与健康相关时才认为它们很重要？”

paras.en: The Problem With Medicalizing Loneliness
paras.zh: 治疗孤独的问题

paras.en: To understand how loneliness became a medical concern, Hiltner conducted interviews with experts and reviewed more than a decade of media coverage, medical journal articles, and academic literature.
paras.zh: 为了了解孤独如何成为一个医学问题，希尔特纳采访了专家，并回顾了十多年的媒体报道、医学期刊文章和学术文献。

paras.en: Her analysis revealed that establishing a connection between loneliness and poor health helped the issue gain credibility. However, it also encouraged what she describes as a "logical leap": the belief that any problem affecting human health should become the responsibility of the healthcare system.
paras.zh: 她的分析显示，在孤独和健康状况不佳之间建立联系有助于这个问题获得可信度。然而，这也鼓励了她所说的“逻辑飞跃”：相信任何影响人类健康的问题都应该成为医疗保健系统的责任。

paras.en: "Not everything that relates to health belongs in healthcare," she said. "Doctors can screen patients and connect them to services, but they cannot rebuild communities or shorten work hours."
paras.zh: “并非所有与健康相关的事情都属于医疗保健，”她说。 “医生可以筛查患者并为他们提供服务，但他们无法重建社区或缩短工作时间。”

paras.en: Hiltner, a predoctoral trainee in social demography at the Population Studies Center within the University of Michigan's Institute for Social Research, was inspired to investigate loneliness after witnessing her grandmother become increasingly isolated as she aged.
paras.zh: 希尔特纳是密歇根大学社会研究所人口研究中心的社会人口学博士前实习生，在目睹祖母随着年龄的增长而变得越来越孤立后，她受到启发，开始研究孤独感。

paras.en: When Hiltner entered graduate school to research social isolation among older adults, she learned that clinical trials were investigating a "loneliness pill." The discovery prompted her to question why loneliness was being approached primarily as a medical condition rather than a social problem.
paras.zh: 当希尔特纳进入研究生院研究老年人的社会隔离时，她得知临床试验正在研究一种“孤独药”。这一发现促使她质疑为什么孤独主要被视为一种医疗状况而不是社会问题。

paras.en: "After my grandfather died, my grandmother lived alone and there was little structure in her life," Hiltner said. "She didn't seem to have many friends or activities. It made me think about everything that happened throughout her life that led to that point. I wondered about the social policies, in addition to dynamics at the family level, that could have helped prevent that situation."
paras.zh: “我的祖父去世后，我的祖母独自生活，她的生活几乎没有什么结构，”希尔特纳说。 “她似乎没有很多朋友或活动。这让我思考她一生中发生的一切导致了这一点。我想知道除了家庭层面的动态之外，社会政策可能有助于防止这种情况。”

paras.en: Finding Solutions Beyond the Healthcare System
paras.zh: 寻找医疗保健系统之外的解决方案

paras.en: Interestingly, Hiltner found that the medical community was initially reluctant to take responsibility for addressing loneliness. Much of the momentum behind incorporating loneliness into healthcare instead came from academic researchers, government health officials, and insurance companies.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，希尔特纳发现医学界最初不愿意承担解决孤独问题的责任。将孤独纳入医疗保健的大部分动力来自学术研究人员、政府卫生官员和保险公司。

paras.en: Although recognizing loneliness as a medical concern can generate greater awareness and encourage intervention, it may also divert valuable resources from efforts to address the social circumstances that leave people isolated.
paras.zh: 尽管认识到孤独是一种医学问题可以提高人们的认识并鼓励干预，但它也可能会转移用于解决导致人们孤立的社会环境的宝贵资源。

paras.en: "There is the risk that defining loneliness as medical crowds out other ways of responding to the issue," she said. "Attention, time and resources are limited. On the other hand, framing it as medical may inspire more action than would have otherwise happened."
paras.zh: 她说：“将孤独定义为医疗人群，可能会排除其他应对这一问题的方法。” “注意力、时间和资源都是有限的。另一方面，将其界定为医学可能会激发比其他情况下更多的行动。”
